office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Victoria Garcia Wilburn
incumbent.summary: Victoria Garcia Wilburn, a Fishers Democrat and Indiana University associate professor of occupational therapy, was first elected in 2022; the House Democratic caucus lists her as ranking minority member of the Judiciary Committee and a member of the Employment, Labor and Pensions and Public Health committees [3, 4].
record: April 2025: Voted no on Senate Bill 1, the 2025 property-tax law, saying Hamilton County stood to lose $132.98 million and that local income taxes could rise; also voted no on the 2025 state budget (HEA 1001), citing public-school, public-health and pre-K funding, while saying she supported its cigarette-tax increase [5, 6].

December 5, 2025: Voted no on House Bill 1032, the mid-decade congressional redistricting bill, which passed the House 57-41; she said she voted no because of "an outpouring of calls and emails from constituents" opposing it [7, 8].

2026 session: Authored House Bill 1036, requiring Department of Child Services caseworkers to see a child in person before closing a case; the bill passed both chambers unanimously and was signed into law, according to her office [9, 10].

2026: Her request for an interim study of guardian ad litem and court-appointed special advocate programs was approved, and in August she called on FSSA to pause procedural Medicaid terminations in counties hit by flooding [11, 12].

race_context: House District 32 covers parts of Fishers, Carmel and a small part of Indianapolis, crossing Hamilton and Marion counties, according to LarryInFishers and Garcia Wilburn's campaign [13, 14].
Garcia Wilburn won the seat in 2022 and was re-elected in 2024 with 52.1% of the vote, according to Wikipedia [15, 16].
No Republican filed for the May 2026 primary; on June 26, 2026, Hamilton County Republican precinct committee members chose Paul Nix by unanimous vote in a caucus to fill the ballot vacancy [17, 13].
No debate or forum between the two candidates was found as of October 10, 2026.

Property taxes are a point of difference: Garcia Wilburn voted against the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1), saying it would cut local services and raise local income taxes, while Nix calls the law's $300 credit inadequate and supports a proposal to replace property taxes with a 7% tax on services [5, 18].

candidates.summary: Paul Nix, the Republican nominee, is a Fishers insurance agent picked by a party caucus in June 2026 who is running mainly on eliminating property taxes [13, 18].
background: Has worked in insurance for more than 40 years, largely with senior clients, and has served as a vice precinct committeeman, according to LarryInFishers [13].
Moved to Fishers from Fort Wayne in 1990 and lives in Delaware Township [18, 13].
Ran for the seat in 2022, finishing third in the Republican primary with 479 votes (about 11.5%) [13].
path_to_ballot: Was chosen on June 26, 2026 by a unanimous vote of Hamilton County Republican precinct committee members at a caucus held to fill the vacancy left when no Republican filed for the primary [17, 13].

items: His campaign says Hoosiers are "being taxed out of homes they already own" and calls for "real reform" rather than "a $300 credit that disappears from local increases" [18].

Supports House Bill 1288, a proposal by Rep. J.D. Prescott to abolish property taxes and replace them with a 7% tax on services; in a letter to The Reporter he wrote that state fiscal estimates showed it would raise more revenue than property taxes [19, 18].
Says he would keep a balanced budget and "find real savings in programs like Medicaid and Medicare without cutting the quality of care" [18].
Says parents should have the final say in what children are taught; opposes CRT, DEI and "gender ideology" in schools and opposes male athletes competing in girls' sports [18].
In his letter, suggested Hamilton Southeastern Schools, which he said has 1,500 fewer students than six years ago, could rent out empty classrooms "instead of a referendum" [19].
Says he supports legal immigration "100 percent" [18].
Opposes taxpayer funding of abortion and says Indiana should do more to protect the unborn [18].

on_incumbent: No statements by Nix about Garcia Wilburn's record were found; his campaign says District 32 "can be won" and that Indiana under Republican leadership is "the envy of our neighboring States" [18].
At the caucus, he said a candidate who waits until Medicare age to run is "not the typical career politician" [17].
plans: Lists cutting property taxes as his top priority, saying "no Hoosier should ever be evicted from a home they own because they cannot pay the property taxes" [18].
gaps: No endorsements or campaign finance totals were found.
Current Publishing's July 8, 2026 article on the race (youarecurrent.com) could not be read (403).
LarryInFishers summarized positions from Nix's 2022 Ballotpedia survey; Ballotpedia itself could not be read.

candidates.summary: Rep. Victoria Garcia Wilburn, the Democratic incumbent seeking a third term, is an occupational therapist and Indiana University faculty member who has focused on health care, child welfare and public safety training [3, 13].
background: Associate professor of occupational therapy at Indiana University-Indianapolis; earned a bachelor's in occupational therapy from Boston University and master's and doctoral degrees in health science from the University of Indianapolis [4, 3].
Has served on the boards of the American Occupational Therapy Association and Hope Academy Recovery High School, according to the caucus [3].
path_to_ballot: Was unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary [20, 15].

items: Voted against 2025's SEA 1, saying, "Senate Bill 1 in its current form is just not workable for House District 32," and citing potential local income-tax increases and cuts to schools and public safety [5].
Opposed the 2025 budget in part because it moves to universal private school vouchers in 2027 and, she said, did not give special education enough of an increase [6].
Held an education town hall in Fishers in September 2026 [21].

Authored 2026 bills to let patients pick a physical or occupational therapist as a primary care provider (HB 1016) and to require the insurance commissioner to consider affordability when reviewing premium increases (HB 1037) [22].
Has criticized FSSA over Medicaid disenrollments, saying, "FSSA is doing too much too fast" [23].
Opposed mid-decade redistricting, saying in October 2025 that the state should focus on energy bills, property taxes and health care costs instead [24, 8].

Her campaign says she supports first responders and "common sense gun laws"; the caucus says her first-term law (Public Law 139) provides mental health and resiliency training to public safety professionals [14, 3].

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No public statements by Garcia Wilburn about her challenger were found.
plans: Her campaign says she is running to strengthen public schools with attention to special education, improve mental and behavioral health infrastructure and advocate for gun safety laws [14].
endorsements_finance: Endorsed by the OneZone Business Action Committee in March 2026 [20].
Joined NewDEAL, a national network of Democratic state and local officials, in July 2026 [4].
gaps: No campaign finance totals were found.
LarryInFishers described her as a physical therapist; her caucus bio and other sources say occupational therapist.
